mechanism: During monotone tree-value updates, cache each local OT primal plan and dual potentials. If the continuation-cost increment is nonnegative and zero on the cached plan support, the old primal and dual still certify the updated OT exactly, so the local LP is omitted.
omitted_computation: A full unregularized transport solve at every cached parent whose changed child entries do not meet its optimal coupling support; detection uses the sparse change set and an inverse support index.
assumptions: Child lower values increase monotonically under cumulative activation
Cached primal marginals and dual feasibility pass numerical audit
Updates and cached supports have a charged sparse inverse index
Every failed reuse test falls back to the same exact local OT kernel
All preprocessing, index, replay and fallback work is counted
lemma_or_invariant: Let pi and (alpha,beta) be primal/dual optimal for M. If Delta>=0 and sum(pi*Delta)=0, the old dual remains feasible for M+Delta and the old primal cost is unchanged; equality therefore certifies pi optimal for M+Delta. Reuse leaves the clamped Bellman value exact.

nearest_prior_art.remaining_question: Whether sparse inverse-support propagation across an adapted-OT Bellman tree yields a distinct algorithm and certificate-cost reduction

nearest_prior_art.overlap: Incremental affected-ancestor updates in heuristic dynamic programming
nearest_prior_art.remaining_question: Exact reuse of a transport block without resolving its continuous action

prediction: On preregistered fixtures with localized cumulative child-value updates, cached certificates skip at least 50% of eligible local OT solves while reproducing the no-reuse incremental AO-OT values within 1e-9. Detection and index work is below 25% of skipped transport constraint-entry work.
falsification_rule: Any invalid reused witness or value/root mismatch above 1e-9 is implementation_invalid. If correctness passes but a skip/work threshold fails, falsify only that declared performance prediction; infer no impossibility for dynamic OT reuse or tree algorithms.

probe.oracle: Fresh same-kernel local OT is run only after each decision for audit, never used by the reuse decision, and reported separately.
probe.cost_accounting: Count changed entries, inverse-index visits, cached support entries, primal/dual replay, fallback LP dimensions/nonzeros, h, controller work and root-gap evolution on identical update traces.
probe.grid: Fixture-scale only until independent review; both costs, k=1/2, branching/recombining trees, support-hit/miss updates, zero masses and degenerate optimal faces.

breadth_challenge: The lemma is cost/process agnostic, but performance depends on locality and support hits. Survival must next cross both frozen processes, both costs and k=1/2 before T=50.
ablation: Identical update trace and OT kernel: cached AO-OT without reuse; support-disjoint reuse; dense scan versus inverse support index.
unresolved_objections: The lemma is elementary LP sensitivity and may not be novel
Updates may hit most cached supports
Index maintenance may cost as much as sparse local OT
Degenerate optimal faces may make one cached plan a poor witness
Float64 equality needs residual correction or outward audit
